rationale: R10 (M60 standing rule, rust #798): a relationship TARGET must be spelled the way the lane spells its own symbols — plus the one row the F14 gate added when it was extended to rust: `calls -> Self`, a KEYWORD published as a callee name (the lane refuses `Self` as a name on the read surface and resolves it on the instantiates surface, so the `calls` surface was an inconsistency, and 6 cargo rows came from `Ok(Self(name))` / `Self(ProcessEnv)`). An impl symbol is named after the TYPE it implements, and a reference/pointer/parenthesized wrapper does not change what that type is NAMED — the pre-fix rule took `typeNode.text` verbatim, so `impl ChannelChangerCommandExt for &mut ProcessBuilder` published the source TEXT `&mut ProcessBuilder` as a name: on the impl SYMBOL, on the `implements` edge's SOURCE, on each member's owner, and (through `Self`) on every `references` target inside the block. The M60 target-spelling census convicted rust for exactly this (6 `references` targets over 2 files on the 667-file draw). The differential is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to it (its truth derives from the same rule — both sides spelled the fabrication identically), so this fixture and the F14 gate are the independent evidence. Every forbid below was re-derived from HEAD's analyzer (script/m14/tmp/rust-798-fixture-dump.ts with BB_PRE_R10=1), which printed for this very file: symbols `&mut ProcessBuilder|impl`, `&'static str|impl`, `(T, U)|impl`, `[u8]|impl`; `implements|&mut ProcessBuilder|ChannelChangerCommandExt`, `implements|&'static str|IntoUrl`, `implements|(T, U)|ToTupleId`, `implements|[u8]|ToSliceId`; and `references|env|&mut ProcessBuilder`, `references|into_url|&'static str`, `references|to_tuple_id|(T, U)`, `references|to_slice_id|[u8]` (the last two wrong even in SPELLING: a target no consumer can resolve). So each forbid provably FAILS on revert, and the R10 mutant (rust/revert-impl-target-wrapper-name) exercises it. THREE RULINGS the file also pins: (1) `&'static str` is the WRAPPED primitive `str`; (2) `std::io::Error` is the QUALIFIED case and its qualification is PRESERVED on the symbol while `Self` resolves to the LEAF `Error` — a deliberate pre-existing asymmetry, because the deferred constructor filter reads in-file SYMBOL names and flattening a foreign `io::Error` to `Error` would make `Error::new()` look like a local construction (measured: it added 12 spurious `instantiates` edges on ripgrep alone); (3) a type with NO nominal name (`(T, U)`, `[u8]`) gets the family's declared synthetic `anonymous_impl` with the source spelling in `metadata.implementedType`, while `Self` resolves to ABSENCE — the R7 rule that the honest state is absence, not a placeholder, and the synthetic block name is never substituted for the type in a TARGET position. SUPERSESSION (2026-10-19, Lead decision §21.11 task-36 defect 1, task-9 conditions): the impl block used to be published under the TYPE'S OWN NAME (`kind: impl`, name `ProcessBuilder`), which put a duplicate declaration next to `struct ProcessBuilder` in the project key space — `struct Foo` + `impl Foo` read as TWO declarations, so the unique-bare-name rule refused `Foo` everywhere (the measured 1,672-row instantiates artifact and same-file ambiguity across instantiates/exports/references/uses). The block is a CONTAINER, not a declaration of the type: its published identity is now the distinct `<Type>::r#impl`, its members are owned by the NOMINAL type (checked by the `contains` rows below), and the `implements` edge keeps the type as its SOURCE. R10's naming contract is therefore observable at exactly these surfaces and the duplicate identities are now FORBIDDEN explicitly rather than being part of the symbol surface.
